implementation_notes: Promise is part of the language (ES2015) with async/await added in ES2017: a promise is a proxy for a value not necessarily known when it is created, it runs through pending -> fulfilled|rejected exactly once, and its handlers are always invoked from the job queue, so attaching after settlement is safe. The write end is the executor's resolve/reject (or returning from an async function), composition is then/catch/finally chaining or await, and fan-in is Promise.all/allSettled/any/race with the keyed variants; the language has no first-class cancellation, so the operation itself must be cancellable through an AbortController/AbortSignal, and the classic promise/future structure only reappears when a callback API is wrapped by hand.
pitfalls: Unhandled rejections become global errors (and terminate a Node process): every chain needs a terminal catch, and Promise.race leaves its handlers attached to a never-settling promise - promises provide no way to unsubscribe them.
Handlers never run synchronously but in a later job, so 'resolved' does not mean 'visible in this tick' - code written as if settlement were immediate observes stale state.
await in a loop serialises the iterations (each await yields a microtask turn): fan out with Promise.all instead of awaiting one after another.
